label: Follow the Flow
line: One question tied to something the viewer does, then the parts in the order things happen, each term named only after its job, closed by a callback to the action.
best_for: a process with a natural order: a request, a boot, a login, a payment, a signal through the body
a 'what really happens when you' topic
also_for: a weakness or an attack that proceeds step by step
a mechanism with no paradox and no visible failure
avoid_for: a classification with no order (record types, permission bits): follow one example through, or use a ladder
a process that needs three ideas explained before anything moves
signals: the subject moves through stages in a fixed order
each stage hands something to the next
the topic is phrased as what happens when
the interest is in the steps, with no paradox and no failure

beats.name: The action
beats.job: The viewer does the thing, and the first step is already moving.

beats.name: Stage 1
beats.job: The first part, in the order the system itself works, with a count if there is one.

beats.name: Stages 2 to 4
beats.job: One or two sentences each. What it does first, its name second. One contrast or one corrected misconception on the way.

beats.name: Last stage
beats.job: The most vivid or most surprising stage, kept for last.

beats.name: Callback
beats.job: Back to the action the script opened on, in one clause. Then stop.

hooks.shape: What really happens when you [everyday action]?
You [do the everyday action]. Before [short time] is up, [the first thing] has already [happened].
[Everyday action] takes [a count] of [steps or hops] and about [a short time].

holds: The count or the path is the progress bar: the viewer always knows how far the end is. The pull is 'what happens next to me', so no extra question has to be made up. The biggest obstacle or the strangest stage goes last.
ending: The last stage's detail, or the callback to the action. Never a summary of the stages.
pitfalls: Name, then definition, then example, repeated for every part
Stopping the flow for a background lesson
A question opening under a publish title that asks the same question: title the video with the surprising stage, and let the opening ask
template: What really happens when you [action]? It starts when [first thing]. First, [part] [does its job]: that is [its name]. Next, [part 2] [checks or transforms]. Many people think [misconception]; in fact [fact]. Then [part 3] [hands over]. Last, [the final stage, its most vivid detail]. Every time you [action].
